title: P3 - Durable connector inbox and outbox
outcome: Signed inbound events land in a transactional inbox where a unique deduplication key decides which single transaction starts a mission, replacing a receipt file and a lock released before the work begins. Outbound connector actions are written to an outbox in the same transaction as the evidence they record, and are delivered by a worker with exponential backoff, jitter, honoured retry hints and an attempt cap that ends in a dead-letter queue rather than a dropped exception.
notInScope: No change to signature verification on ingress. No new connectors. Exactly-once reply is effective, not absolute: it rests on connector-specific idempotency markers, and where a connector cannot be queried for a marker the behaviour degrades to a retry with a visible duplicate annotation rather than a silent second message.
completionEvidence: A duplicate-webhook test posts five concurrent correctly signed requests and asserts exactly one mission directory exists. A connector-retry test drives a fake endpoint that answers 429 with a retry hint twice and then 200, and asserts exactly one reply was delivered. A crash variant sets the crash point after the post and asserts that restart verifies the in-flight row by marker query and does not send a second message. Tests that asserted on receipt files are consciously rewritten to assert on inbox rows, and that rewrite is stated in the pull request rather than absorbed.

metadata.risk: Marker-based exactly-once delivery is connector-specific. GitHub ships first because a hidden marker in a comment body can be queried back. Slack and Jira follow. Where a marker cannot be read back the plan degrades honestly and says so in the operator documentation, rather than claiming a guarantee the connector does not support.
